fixtures.lesson: One atom has a unique minimal p-world; rank remains ordinal rather than probabilistic.
Two minimal worlds disagree on p, preserving an explicit counterexample to entailment.
Three atoms create four ordinal layers and a nontrivial conjunctive revision target.
The input p and not-p has no worlds, so revision availability remains explicitly false.
A disjunctive input exposes how bounded revision policies can select different rank projections.
